## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2009-08-27: S-1/A Amendment No. 6 first attaches the form-of TRA (Exhibit 10.4)
- 2009-09-29: Up-C IPO closes; original TRA executed among Artio Global Investors Inc., Artio Global Holdings LLC, Pell, and Younes

#### Aberdeen merger and Amended and Restated TRA

- 2012-02-29: 10-K discloses first TRA payment of approximately $5.0 million to Principals
- 2013-02-13: 8-K reports Aberdeen merger agreement; Amended and Restated TRA executed concurrently, substituting Aberdeen Asset Management Inc. as Corporation post-close and adding closing-date accelerated payments
- 2013-03-04: 10-K discloses $141.6M valuation-allowance-driven reduction in the TRA liability
- 2013-05-21: Aberdeen merger closes; A&R TRA becomes effective under its Section 7.14; Artio subsequently deregisters

## Explanation

Artio Global Investors completed its Up-C IPO on September 29, 2009 and executed an 85% Tax Receivable Agreement with the two firm Principals, Richard C. Pell and Rudolph-Riad Younes, covering cash tax savings from Section 754 basis step-ups generated by future exchanges of Artio Global Holdings LLC units. By year-end 2012, a $178.5 million valuation allowance against the underlying deferred tax asset reduced the recorded TRA liability by $141.6 million but did not terminate the contract. Concurrent with the February 2013 Aberdeen merger agreement, the parties signed an Amended and Restated TRA substituting Aberdeen Asset Management Inc. as Corporation, preserving the ultimate 85%/15% economic split, and adding closing-date accelerated payments for the 2012 tax year, the 2011 NOL carryback refund, and 2013 partial-year benefits. Aberdeen completed the acquisition on May 21, 2013 and the contract continues under Aberdeen's reporting, which is outside this CIK's filings. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
